title: Tech Note: Preventing Web Users from Downloading Pictures
author: Chiheb Nasr, 4D S.A.
featured_technology: 4DACTION-served image delivery (SEND HTML BLOB of PICTURE TO GIF)
Time-window URL replay protection (comparing Current time to an embedded timestamp)
4dvar tag for embedding a dynamic image-fetch URL in an tag

historical_commentary.text: Chiheb Nasr (4D S.A.) shows a two-layer scheme to discourage casual downloading of images served by 4D's web server: a browser-side JavaScript handler that blocks right-click/context-menu access to elements, and a server-side 4D check that compares the current time to a timestamp embedded in the 4DACTION image-fetch URL, rejecting requests made too long after the page was generated (to defeat users who copy the raw image URL from View Source). The note is explicit up front that none of this actually prevents image copying (screenshots, cache inspection, drag-and-drop all still work), and today both halves of the technique are essentially obsolete: browsers have moved away from relying on right-click-blocking JavaScript as any kind of protection, and real image protection now relies on watermarking, DRM, or simply accepting that browser-rendered images can always be captured.
related_updates: Right-click/context-menu-blocking JavaScript is now a well-known, easily bypassed anti-pattern rather than a real protection technique
Modern approaches to protecting web images rely on watermarking, licensing/DRM, or server-side access control rather than client-side click interception
